hero.title: White
hero.tagline: Safety is built, not assumed.
hero.thesis: White believes peace is not a mood. It is a structure: rules that hold, shelter that lasts, and obligations people can trust under pressure.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you value shared standards, protection of the vulnerable, dependable obligations, and group safety over private exception.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: White challenges Black's self-priority and Red's unrestrained immediacy, while Green can question whether White's systems listen to living reality.
Check the boundary
This is less likely to fit if you treat rules as inherently oppressive, believe private power owes nothing to others, or want impulse to outrank communal safety.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The shelter-builder
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents feel the deck as a standard made tangible: removal, protection, and board presence all answer the same question of safety.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through protection, structure, and the feeling that someone thought about what happens after the hit lands.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
shelter, duty, standards, and collective protection
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Board wipes, token makers, protection spells, taxes, and equipment that turns safety into enforceable tempo
TABLE EXPERIENCE
reliable protection, disciplined pressure, and structure that keeps returning to the board

Lines of Magic flavor that sound like this reading.

EXACT CARD VOICE
When hearts and minds align, so too do actions.
VIEW CARD DETAILS

EXACT CARD VOICE

Cards whose verified play patterns give you a concrete way to explore this reading.

WHY IT FITS IN PLAY
Giada gives White's coordinated creature growth a direct example: she helps cast Angels, and each later Angel enters with counters for the Angels already assembled.

hero.title: Blue
hero.tagline: Possibility opens when the pattern is understood.
hero.thesis: Blue believes no one is finished by default. Knowledge, practice, and precise systems let people and worlds become more than their starting shape.
hero.art_credit: ART: ZOLTAN BOROS & GABOR SZIKSZAI - ACADEMY RUINS

panels.text:
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Blue is a Commander deck that turns knowledge into control: draw cards, preserve options, answer key spells, and let information become inevitability. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Draw-Go Control, Spellslinger Tokens, Artifacts and Clones. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
COLOR SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether to hold up Draw-Go Control, turn spells into token pressure, or build around artifacts and copied effects, then decide how much mana must stay available each turn.
TABLE CAUTION
Hold mana for the important spell, draw before committing, and keep one clean answer for the table's real threat.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you study before committing, build models, practice deliberately, and want tools or education to overcome starting limits.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: Blue challenges Red's immediate feeling and Green's acceptance of the given, while Black asks whether knowledge produces usable agency.
Check the boundary
Mono-Blue is a false center if instinct, fate, or the present impulse should be final and further understanding only delays truth.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The patient planner
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents see cards held back, information gathered, and answers used at the moment they matter.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through open mana, card selection, and flexible answers that keep several routes available.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
knowledge, information, education, experimentation, tools, and deliberate improvement
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Card draw and filtering, counterspells, copying, bounce, theft, flying, artifacts, and instant-and-sorcery play
TABLE EXPERIENCE
held mana, careful selection, flexible interaction, and turns shaped by timing rather than raw force
CARDS THAT SOUND LIKE THIS

Lines of Magic flavor that sound like this reading.

Azami, Lady of Scrolls
EXACT CARD VOICE
"Choices belong to those with the luxuries of time and distance. We have neither. I recommend we proceed with the plan to destroy all shrines of the kami." —Lady Azami, letter to Sensei Hisoka
VIEW CARD DETAILS
April O'Neil, Live on the Scene
EXACT CARD VOICE
"This is great! I must really be onto something hot if they're trying to kill me!"
VIEW CARD DETAILS
CARDS THAT PLAY LIKE THIS
Cards whose verified play patterns give you a concrete way to explore this reading.

WHY IT FITS IN PLAY
Talrand turns Blue's instant-and-sorcery plan into a visible board by creating a flying Drake whenever you cast one of those spells.

records.full_rendered_text:
REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Blue
Possibility opens when the pattern is understood.
Blue believes no one is finished by default. Knowledge, practice, and precise systems let people and worlds become more than their starting shape.
ART: ZOLTAN BOROS & GABOR SZIKSZAI - ACADEMY RUINS
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE
IDENTITY & PLAY
COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Blue is a Commander deck that turns knowledge into control: draw cards, preserve options, answer key spells, and let information become inevitability. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Draw-Go Control, Spellslinger Tokens, Artifacts and Clones. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
COLOR SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether to hold up Draw-Go Control, turn spells into token pressure, or build around artifacts and copied effects, then decide how much mana must stay available each turn.
TABLE CAUTION
Hold mana for the important spell, draw before committing, and keep one clean answer for the table's real threat.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you study before committing, build models, practice deliberately, and want tools or education to overcome starting limits.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: Blue challenges Red's immediate feeling and Green's acceptance of the given, while Black asks whether knowledge produces usable agency.
Check the boundary
Mono-Blue is a false center if instinct, fate, or the present impulse should be final and further understanding only delays truth.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The patient planner
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents see cards held back, information gathered, and answers used at the moment they matter.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through open mana, card selection, and flexible answers that keep several routes available.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
knowledge, information, education, experimentation, tools, and deliberate improvement
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Card draw and filtering, counterspells, copying, bounce, theft, flying, artifacts, and instant-and-sorcery play
TABLE EXPERIENCE
held mana, careful selection, flexible interaction, and turns shaped by timing rather than raw force

hero.title: Black
hero.tagline: Power is protection when no one is coming to save you.
hero.thesis: Black believes the world offers no guaranteed fairness. It secures agency by treating life, death, loyalty, and resources as costs that can be paid for control.

panels.text:
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Black is a Commander deck that turns cost into agency: spend life, cash in creatures, and make the graveyard or hand become a resource engine before the table can stabilize. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Life Payment Engines, Aristocrats and Sacrifice, Reanimator Control. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
COLOR SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether life, sacrificed creatures, or the graveyard is the main fuel source, then keep the recovery line that lets the deck survive its own costs.
TABLE CAUTION
Hold a sacrifice outlet, spend life deliberately, and rebuild from the graveyard before the engine runs dry.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you accept hard costs, refuse to wait for fairness, and convert resources, loss, loyalty, or death into self-determination.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: Black challenges White's group-first morality and Green's destiny/acceptance, while Red shares individualism but rejects excessive calculation.
Check the boundary
Mono-Black is a false center if power must never serve the self, paying a cost is inherently corrupt, or dependence is always more virtuous than agency.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The resource converter
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents see life, cards, creatures, and the graveyard treated as resources whose costs are chosen deliberately.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through sacrifice, life payment, removal, recursion, and the willingness to pay for leverage.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
agency, opportunity, calculated cost, self-advocacy, and resource conversion
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Creature destruction, discard, sacrifice, reanimation, graveyard use, life as a cost, drain, and paid card draw
TABLE EXPERIENCE
costs converted into options, lost pieces returned to use, and leverage preserved through difficult exchanges
CARDS THAT SOUND LIKE THIS

EXACT CARD VOICE

EXACT CARD VOICE

WHY IT FITS IN PLAY
K'rrik makes Black's resource-conversion pattern literal by letting life pay for black mana symbols and rewarding additional black spells with +1/+1 counters.

records.full_rendered_text:
REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Black
Power is protection when no one is coming to save you.
Black believes the world offers no guaranteed fairness. It secures agency by treating life, death, loyalty, and resources as costs that can be paid for control.
ART: DONATO GIANCOLA - ALTAR'S REAP
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE

COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Black is a Commander deck that turns cost into agency: spend life, cash in creatures, and make the graveyard or hand become a resource engine before the table can stabilize. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Life Payment Engines, Aristocrats and Sacrifice, Reanimator Control. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
COLOR SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether life, sacrificed creatures, or the graveyard is the main fuel source, then keep the recovery line that lets the deck survive its own costs.
TABLE CAUTION
Hold a sacrifice outlet, spend life deliberately, and rebuild from the graveyard before the engine runs dry.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you accept hard costs, refuse to wait for fairness, and convert resources, loss, loyalty, or death into self-determination.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: Black challenges White's group-first morality and Green's destiny/acceptance, while Red shares individualism but rejects excessive calculation.
Check the boundary
Mono-Black is a false center if power must never serve the self, paying a cost is inherently corrupt, or dependence is always more virtuous than agency.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The resource converter
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents see life, cards, creatures, and the graveyard treated as resources whose costs are chosen deliberately.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through sacrifice, life payment, removal, recursion, and the willingness to pay for leverage.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
agency, opportunity, calculated cost, self-advocacy, and resource conversion
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Creature destruction, discard, sacrifice, reanimation, graveyard use, life as a cost, drain, and paid card draw
TABLE EXPERIENCE
costs converted into options, lost pieces returned to use, and leverage preserved through difficult exchanges

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you trust emotion as information, act before overthinking kills the moment, and value freedom from artificial restraint.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: Red challenges White's security and Blue's deliberation, while Black can sharpen its self-interest and Green can root its intuition.
Check the boundary
Mono-Red is a false center if every variable must be approved, feeling is unreliable by definition, or safety always outranks the living moment.

AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The first mover
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents see damage, haste, and temporary openings turned into action before the table can settle.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through immediacy, direct damage, speed, impulse access, and short windows that demand an answer now.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
freedom, emotion, impulse, authenticity, and direct action
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Direct damage, haste, temporary mana and power, impulse draw, attack pressure, and effects that matter immediately
TABLE EXPERIENCE
fast commitment, visible momentum, and turns that use the available opening before it closes

hero.tagline: Law, procedure, and enforceable structure protect civic order when they stay accountable to the people they govern.
hero.thesis: Azorius trusts law, information, documentation, and procedure to make civic life legible and protected, while recognizing that process must remain accountable to people.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you trust documented rules, precedent, enforceable fairness, and institutions that prevent harm before crisis.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It distrusts private exceptions, impulsive intervention, and justice that cannot be made legible to everyone.
Check the boundary
A rule-breaker, secret broker, or battlefield protector is not necessarily Azorius; the distinguishing question is whether public procedure remains the accountable method.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The arbiter
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
A rule-setting Azorius list can ask opponents to plan around visible taxes, held mana, or timing constraints; the actual experience depends on the cards, pilot, and pod.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Can create pressure through permission and timing, without proving that the pilot wants a long game or that opponents will react in one fixed way.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
senate, judiciary, and lawkeeping bureaucracy
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Detain, taxation, permission, sweepers, tempo, and rule-setting permanents
TABLE EXPERIENCE
restricted action, procedural pressure, and clean enforcement

Azorius Senate
Law, procedure, and enforceable structure protect civic order when they stay accountable to the people they govern.
Azorius trusts law, information, documentation, and procedure to make civic life legible and protected, while recognizing that process must remain accountable to people.

records.full_rendered_text:
REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Boros Legion
Public protection. Disciplined action.
Boros philosophy joins civic order with urgent protection. Its best expression acts when harm is present, but remains accountable to the public duty it claims to serve.
ART: ADAM PAQUETTE - SOLAR BLAZE
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE
IDENTITY & PLAY
COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Boros Legion is a Commander deck that turns attacks into clean decisions: build one disciplined combat line, protect it, and use equipment or coordinated pressure to end hesitation. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Battalion Formation, Mentor the Front Line, Equipped Protection. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether a Battalion formation, a Mentor-led front line, or one equipped protector carries the attack, then reserve protection for the piece that keeps the public duty intact.
TABLE CAUTION
Sequence attacks carefully, protect your key threat, and remove the blocker that makes the clean strike fail.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you want visible harm answered now, value loyalty and moral clarity, and accept discipline when it makes protection effective.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It resists bureaucratic delay, moral ambiguity used as an excuse, and rules that shield the wrong people.
Check the boundary
Combat, equipment, soldiers, and righteous anger do not establish Boros by themselves; force becomes Boros-specific when it serves accountable public protection and team duty.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The responder
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents see the deck coming. That is part of the point: the line is public, and crossing it has consequences.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through action, retaliation, combat, and visible protection.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
security force, constabulary, and army
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Battalion, mentor, tactical combat, equipment, burn, and protection
TABLE EXPERIENCE
coordinated pressure, righteous retaliation, and visible action

hero.title: Cult of Rakdos
hero.tagline: Performance makes appetite, cost, and consequence visible.
hero.thesis: Rakdos turns black-red appetite into public spectacle: performance, provocation, sensation, and visible cost become the way restraint is mocked and hidden pressure is exposed. It is not generic evil or random disruption; the signal is the act, the audience, and the consequence.

panels.text:
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Cult of Rakdos is a Commander deck that makes entertainment expensive: push damage, cash in reckless advantage, and turn spectacle into a pressure engine the table has to respect. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Spectacle Pressure, Risk for Release, Sacrifice with Consequence. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Damage triggers, sacrifice outlets, impulse draw, menace threats, and chaos payoffs that make opponents pay for every seat in the room.
TABLE CAUTION
Sequence smaller threats first, make the table spend removal, then turn the damage engine loose.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you value performance, provocation, sensation, release, and an act whose audience can see both intensity and cost.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It rejects respectability, hidden pressure, and restraint that disguises what people actually want.
Check the boundary
This is less likely to fit if the deck offers only private cruelty, ordinary aggression, sacrifice mechanics, or random chaos without an act, audience, or visible consequence.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The spectacle engine
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents feel the deck as a dare: life totals, resources, and caution all become part of the show.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through risk, damage, sacrifice, and ecstatic escalation.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
performance cult, riotous stage, and thrill economy
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Spectacle, sacrifice, impulse draw, menace, damage triggers, and reckless advantage
TABLE EXPERIENCE
volatile pressure, public risk, and turns that make the room react
CARDS THAT SOUND LIKE THIS

EXACT CARD VOICE

records.full_rendered_text:
REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Cult of Rakdos
Performance makes appetite, cost, and consequence visible.
Rakdos turns black-red appetite into public spectacle: performance, provocation, sensation, and visible cost become the way restraint is mocked and hidden pressure is exposed. It is not generic evil or random disruption; the signal is the act, the audience, and the consequence.
ART: RIX MAADI, DUNGEON PALACE
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE
IDENTITY & PLAY
COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Cult of Rakdos is a Commander deck that makes entertainment expensive: push damage, cash in reckless advantage, and turn spectacle into a pressure engine the table has to respect. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Spectacle Pressure, Risk for Release, Sacrifice with Consequence. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Damage triggers, sacrifice outlets, impulse draw, menace threats, and chaos payoffs that make opponents pay for every seat in the room.
TABLE CAUTION
Sequence smaller threats first, make the table spend removal, then turn the damage engine loose.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you value performance, provocation, sensation, release, and an act whose audience can see both intensity and cost.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It rejects respectability, hidden pressure, and restraint that disguises what people actually want.
Check the boundary
This is less likely to fit if the deck offers only private cruelty, ordinary aggression, sacrifice mechanics, or random chaos without an act, audience, or visible consequence.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The spectacle engine
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents feel the deck as a dare: life totals, resources, and caution all become part of the show.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through risk, damage, sacrifice, and ecstatic escalation.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
performance cult, riotous stage, and thrill economy
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Spectacle, sacrifice, impulse draw, menace, damage triggers, and reckless advantage
TABLE EXPERIENCE
volatile pressure, public risk, and turns that make the room react

Such is the power of Rakdos that even his shadow takes on a cruel life of its own.

hero.title: Golgari Swarm
hero.tagline: What is discarded can feed the next cycle.
hero.thesis: Golgari treats death, decay, and discarded matter as useful material inside a living cycle: undercity survival, food production, graveyard resources, and renewal rather than generic morbidity.
hero.art_credit: ART: MARK TEDIN - DARK HEART OF THE WOOD

panels.text:
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Golgari Swarm is a Commander deck that turns death into future value: fill the graveyard, sacrifice expendable bodies, and grind through resource loops until every trade becomes reclamation. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Reclamation Midrange, Graveyard Resource Loops, Undergrowth and Renewal. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether reclamation midrange, graveyard resource loops, or Undergrowth and renewal converts loss into material, then keep a recovery line for graveyard hate.
TABLE CAUTION
If graveyard hate appears early, slow down, rebuild through value creatures, and hold your recursion until the table spends its answers.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you find meaning in reclamation, patience, discarded material, self-sustaining cycles, and life emerging from death.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It resists denial of mortality, preservation that blocks renewal, and hierarchies pretending they do not decay.
Check the boundary
Graveyard value, morbidity, resilience, and sacrifice do not establish Golgari by themselves; the distinguishing method is a death-to-life cycle that feeds survival or renewal.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The survivor
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents learn that removal is not an ending; it is the next material the deck will use.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through endurance, reclamation, and the certainty that nothing is wasted.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
waste, agriculture, rot, undercity survival, and reclamation
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Dredge, scavenge, undergrowth, recursion, sacrifice, and graveyard value
TABLE EXPERIENCE
loss converted into future pressure and a board that keeps returning

REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Golgari Swarm
What is discarded can feed the next cycle.
Golgari treats death, decay, and discarded matter as useful material inside a living cycle: undercity survival, food production, graveyard resources, and renewal rather than generic morbidity.
ART: MARK TEDIN - DARK HEART OF THE WOOD
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE
IDENTITY & PLAY
COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Golgari Swarm is a Commander deck that turns death into future value: fill the graveyard, sacrifice expendable bodies, and grind through resource loops until every trade becomes reclamation. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Reclamation Midrange, Graveyard Resource Loops, Undergrowth and Renewal. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether reclamation midrange, graveyard resource loops, or Undergrowth and renewal converts loss into material, then keep a recovery line for graveyard hate.
TABLE CAUTION
If graveyard hate appears early, slow down, rebuild through value creatures, and hold your recursion until the table spends its answers.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you find meaning in reclamation, patience, discarded material, self-sustaining cycles, and life emerging from death.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It resists denial of mortality, preservation that blocks renewal, and hierarchies pretending they do not decay.
Check the boundary
Graveyard value, morbidity, resilience, and sacrifice do not establish Golgari by themselves; the distinguishing method is a death-to-life cycle that feeds survival or renewal.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The survivor
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents learn that removal is not an ending; it is the next material the deck will use.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through endurance, reclamation, and the certainty that nothing is wasted.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
waste, agriculture, rot, undercity survival, and reclamation
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Dredge, scavenge, undergrowth, recursion, sacrifice, and graveyard value
TABLE EXPERIENCE
loss converted into future pressure and a board that keeps returning

The Golgari support a vast army because death never ends its soldiers' service.

A classic Golgari leader who scales with the size of your graveyard and allows you to 'recycle' creatures into direct damage.

hero.title: Gruul Clans
hero.tagline: Wild places lost. The clans answer directly.
hero.thesis: The Gruul were assigned Ravnica's wild places, then urban expansion and other guilds eroded that role. Their red-green identity centers loose clans, Rubblebelt territory, direct action, riot and bloodrush pressure, and anger at imposed civilization.

panels.text:
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Gruul Clans is a Commander deck that attacks the table before it can settle: ramp hard, present oversized trampling threats, and make everyone answer creatures on your pace. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Wild Reclamation, Clan-Fed Pressure, Riot Momentum. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether wild reclamation, clan-fed creature pressure, or Riot momentum carries the attack, then ramp toward the threat that makes imposed pacing impossible.
TABLE CAUTION
Ramp with a destination, sequence smaller threats first, and protect the one oversized creature that makes blocks impossible.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you trust instinct, authenticity, clan, territory, and direct action rooted in a concrete loss or endangered wild place.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It distrusts institutions that broke their promises, abstraction that ignores material damage, and patience demanded by beneficiaries of the system.
Check the boundary
Rage, stompy play, and destruction do not establish Gruul by themselves; look for wildness, territory, clan, or resistance to imposed order.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The breaker of gates
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents see the deck as pressure from outside the city walls: fast, physical, and hard to civilize.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through instinct, oversized threats, and refusal of imposed order.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
clans, wild places, razed boundaries, and anti-civilized resistance
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Riot, bloodrush, ramp, trample, fight spells, and creature pressure
TABLE EXPERIENCE
immediate combat, land-fed force, and damage that refuses delay

records.full_rendered_text:
REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Gruul Clans
Wild places lost. The clans answer directly.
The Gruul were assigned Ravnica's wild places, then urban expansion and other guilds eroded that role. Their red-green identity centers loose clans, Rubblebelt territory, direct action, riot and bloodrush pressure, and anger at imposed civilization.
ART: ADAM PAQUETTE - ZHUR-TAA ANCIENT
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE
IDENTITY & PLAY
COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Gruul Clans is a Commander deck that attacks the table before it can settle: ramp hard, present oversized trampling threats, and make everyone answer creatures on your pace. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Wild Reclamation, Clan-Fed Pressure, Riot Momentum. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether wild reclamation, clan-fed creature pressure, or Riot momentum carries the attack, then ramp toward the threat that makes imposed pacing impossible.
TABLE CAUTION
Ramp with a destination, sequence smaller threats first, and protect the one oversized creature that makes blocks impossible.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you trust instinct, authenticity, clan, territory, and direct action rooted in a concrete loss or endangered wild place.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It distrusts institutions that broke their promises, abstraction that ignores material damage, and patience demanded by beneficiaries of the system.
Check the boundary
Rage, stompy play, and destruction do not establish Gruul by themselves; look for wildness, territory, clan, or resistance to imposed order.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The breaker of gates
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents see the deck as pressure from outside the city walls: fast, physical, and hard to civilize.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through instinct, oversized threats, and refusal of imposed order.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
clans, wild places, razed boundaries, and anti-civilized resistance
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Riot, bloodrush, ramp, trample, fight spells, and creature pressure
TABLE EXPERIENCE
immediate combat, land-fed force, and damage that refuses delay

EXACT CARD VOICE

hero.thesis: Dimir turns information into hidden leverage through secrecy, backroom dealing, observation, and delayed disclosure.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore House Dimir is a Commander deck that wins once the table understands too late: trade in hidden information, mill or discard the right resources, and turn the delayed payoff into a protected finish. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Hidden Information Leverage, Surveil Filtering, Covert Infiltration. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether hidden information, Surveil filtering, or covert infiltration creates the leverage, then decide what stays concealed until the table can no longer stop it.
TABLE CAUTION
Wait until shields drop, hold interaction, and draw cards before revealing the card that actually wins.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you observe first, control disclosure, value anonymity, and prefer advantage that does not require public credit.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It resists transparency as an automatic virtue and visible legitimacy as the only valid form of power.
Check the boundary
Control, mill, theft, and evasive play do not establish Dimir by themselves; secrecy or information asymmetry must be the active method.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The concealed hand
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents rarely know which card matters until it has already taken their best line away.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through uncertainty, hidden advantage, and delayed reveal.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
couriers, archivists, spies, and memory manipulators
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Surveil, mill, discard, theft, evasive threats, and control
TABLE EXPERIENCE
hidden pressure, information advantage, and wins that arrive before the table understands them
CARDS THAT SOUND LIKE THIS

Lines of Magic flavor that sound like this reading.

Consult the Necrosages
EXACT CARD VOICE
Dimir rank and file never see nor hear their guildmaster. All orders are given through mysterious necrosages who appear from the shadows, tersely toss out a command, and then melt into the darkness.
VIEW CARD DETAILS
Barrier of Bones
EXACT CARD VOICE
The Dimir rarely make statements, but when they do, the message is clear.
VIEW CARD DETAILS
CARDS THAT PLAY LIKE THIS
Cards whose verified play patterns give you a concrete way to explore this reading.
Lazav, Dimir Mastermind
WHY IT FITS IN PLAY
When an opponent's creature card reaches their graveyard, Lazav can copy it while keeping his name, legendary status, hexproof, and the ability to copy again.
Clones
Hidden information
Graveyard interaction
VIEW CARD DETAILS

REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
House Dimir
Secrets, backroom deals, and hidden information leverage.
Dimir turns information into hidden leverage through secrecy, backroom dealing, observation, and delayed disclosure.
ART: TOMASZ JEDRUSZEK - MORTUS STRIDER
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE
IDENTITY & PLAY
COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore House Dimir is a Commander deck that wins once the table understands too late: trade in hidden information, mill or discard the right resources, and turn the delayed payoff into a protected finish. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Hidden Information Leverage, Surveil Filtering, Covert Infiltration. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether hidden information, Surveil filtering, or covert infiltration creates the leverage, then decide what stays concealed until the table can no longer stop it.
TABLE CAUTION
Wait until shields drop, hold interaction, and draw cards before revealing the card that actually wins.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you observe first, control disclosure, value anonymity, and prefer advantage that does not require public credit.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It resists transparency as an automatic virtue and visible legitimacy as the only valid form of power.
Check the boundary
Control, mill, theft, and evasive play do not establish Dimir by themselves; secrecy or information asymmetry must be the active method.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The concealed hand
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents rarely know which card matters until it has already taken their best line away.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through uncertainty, hidden advantage, and delayed reveal.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
couriers, archivists, spies, and memory manipulators
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Surveil, mill, discard, theft, evasive threats, and control
TABLE EXPERIENCE
hidden pressure, information advantage, and wins that arrive before the table understands them

EXACT CARD VOICE
Dimir rank and file never see nor hear their guildmaster. All orders are given through mysterious necrosages who appear from the shadows, tersely toss out a command, and then melt into the darkness.

Barrier of Bones
EXACT CARD VOICE
The Dimir rarely make statements, but when they do, the message is clear.

hero.title: Izzet League
hero.tagline: Invent first. Stabilize what the experiment teaches.
hero.thesis: The Izzet League turns blue-red curiosity into elemental magic, mizzium technology, civic engineering, spell engines, and prototypes. Its best work makes discovery useful; its pressure point is volatile experimentation that can outrun care, procedure, or restraint.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Izzet League is a Commander deck that turns velocity into advantage: chain experiments, recur the right spell, and use tempo to make the table answer your storm before it stabilizes. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Prototype Velocity, Jump-Start Iteration, Overload Breakthrough. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether prototype velocity, Jump-start iteration, or an Overload breakthrough is the experiment, then budget the cards and mana that let a failed test teach the next one.
TABLE CAUTION
Wait for shields to drop, hold interaction, and protect the engine before you commit the storm turn.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you follow questions, enjoy prototypes and repeated testing, treat being wrong as information, and prefer the next experiment to the finished answer.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It resists premature closure, untested repetition, and emotional certainty that substitutes for investigation.
Check the boundary
Spellslinger volume, artifacts, and novelty do not establish Izzet by themselves; look for experiment, discovery, prototypes, or a useful breakthrough.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The live experiment
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents feel the deck accelerating in public, where every cantrip might become the turn that matters.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through velocity, improvisation, and spell sequences that refuse to sit still.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
inventors, engineers, experimenters, and dangerous civic infrastructure
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Jump-start, overload, spellslinger, copying, cantrips, artifacts, and tempo
TABLE EXPERIENCE
spell velocity, explosive pivots, and the sense that the device is running while it is built

REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Izzet League
Invent first. Stabilize what the experiment teaches.
The Izzet League turns blue-red curiosity into elemental magic, mizzium technology, civic engineering, spell engines, and prototypes. Its best work makes discovery useful; its pressure point is volatile experimentation that can outrun care, procedure, or restraint.
ART: STEAM VENTS
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE
IDENTITY & PLAY
COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Izzet League is a Commander deck that turns velocity into advantage: chain experiments, recur the right spell, and use tempo to make the table answer your storm before it stabilizes. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Prototype Velocity, Jump-Start Iteration, Overload Breakthrough. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether prototype velocity, Jump-start iteration, or an Overload breakthrough is the experiment, then budget the cards and mana that let a failed test teach the next one.
TABLE CAUTION
Wait for shields to drop, hold interaction, and protect the engine before you commit the storm turn.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you follow questions, enjoy prototypes and repeated testing, treat being wrong as information, and prefer the next experiment to the finished answer.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It resists premature closure, untested repetition, and emotional certainty that substitutes for investigation.
Check the boundary
Spellslinger volume, artifacts, and novelty do not establish Izzet by themselves; look for experiment, discovery, prototypes, or a useful breakthrough.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The live experiment
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents feel the deck accelerating in public, where every cantrip might become the turn that matters.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through velocity, improvisation, and spell sequences that refuse to sit still.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
inventors, engineers, experimenters, and dangerous civic infrastructure
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Jump-start, overload, spellslinger, copying, cantrips, artifacts, and tempo
TABLE EXPERIENCE
spell velocity, explosive pivots, and the sense that the device is running while it is built

hero.title: Orzhov Syndicate
hero.tagline: Debt, deals, and hierarchy made official.
hero.thesis: Orzhov is the white-black Ravnican guild where religious legitimacy, deal-making business, debt, and cartel hierarchy overlap. Vox Mana reads it through collectible obligation and institutional leverage, not generic WB attrition, lifegain/drain, taxes, sacrifice, recursion, or removal mechanics alone.
hero.art_credit: ART: GREG STAPLES - GHOST COUNCIL OF ORZHOVA

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Orzhov Syndicate is a Commander deck that makes every exchange a debt: tax resources, drain life, sacrifice small pieces, and make obligation a pressure engine no opponent can ignore. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Obligation Engines, Payment Pressure, Afterlife Accounts. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether sacrifice records each obligation, taxes make payment unavoidable, or Afterlife tokens keep the account open, then decide how the deck collects without stalling the table.
TABLE CAUTION
Hold a sacrifice outlet, buy time with drains, and remove the key piece before debts turn into a board wipe.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you treat deals, hierarchy, status, repayment, and long consequences as real sources of power.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It distrusts obligation-free sentiment, chaotic power that cannot be collected, and impartial rules that ignore available leverage.
Check the boundary
Lifegain, drain, sacrifice, taxes, and recursion do not establish Orzhov by themselves; look for debt, deals, tithes, hierarchy, or enforceable obligation.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The creditor
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents feel the deck as a ledger: every attack, death, and favor creates a debt that comes due.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through obligation, drain, taxation, and deals that keep their receipts.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
church-bank hierarchy, contracts, afterlife debt, and inherited power
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Extort, afterlife, aristocrats, lifedrain, sacrifice, taxes, and recursion
TABLE EXPERIENCE
transactional pressure, slow drain, and resource exchanges that stop being equal
CARDS THAT SOUND LIKE THIS

Lines of Magic flavor that sound like this reading.

Afterlife Insurance
EXACT CARD VOICE
As far as the Orzhov Syndicate is concerned, it is the height of irresponsibility not to have a plan for your own ghost.
VIEW CARD DETAILS
Covetous Elegy
EXACT CARD VOICE
Wealthier than ever thanks to exorbitant interest on wartime loans, the Orzhov only grew hungrier for more.

REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Orzhov Syndicate
Debt, deals, and hierarchy made official.
Orzhov is the white-black Ravnican guild where religious legitimacy, deal-making business, debt, and cartel hierarchy overlap. Vox Mana reads it through collectible obligation and institutional leverage, not generic WB attrition, lifegain/drain, taxes, sacrifice, recursion, or removal mechanics alone.
ART: GREG STAPLES - GHOST COUNCIL OF ORZHOVA
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE
IDENTITY & PLAY
COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Orzhov Syndicate is a Commander deck that makes every exchange a debt: tax resources, drain life, sacrifice small pieces, and make obligation a pressure engine no opponent can ignore. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Obligation Engines, Payment Pressure, Afterlife Accounts. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether sacrifice records each obligation, taxes make payment unavoidable, or Afterlife tokens keep the account open, then decide how the deck collects without stalling the table.
TABLE CAUTION
Hold a sacrifice outlet, buy time with drains, and remove the key piece before debts turn into a board wipe.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you treat deals, hierarchy, status, repayment, and long consequences as real sources of power.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It distrusts obligation-free sentiment, chaotic power that cannot be collected, and impartial rules that ignore available leverage.
Check the boundary
Lifegain, drain, sacrifice, taxes, and recursion do not establish Orzhov by themselves; look for debt, deals, tithes, hierarchy, or enforceable obligation.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The creditor
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents feel the deck as a ledger: every attack, death, and favor creates a debt that comes due.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through obligation, drain, taxation, and deals that keep their receipts.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
church-bank hierarchy, contracts, afterlife debt, and inherited power
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Extort, afterlife, aristocrats, lifedrain, sacrifice, taxes, and recursion
TABLE EXPERIENCE
transactional pressure, slow drain, and resource exchanges that stop being equal

EXACT CARD VOICE
As far as the Orzhov Syndicate is concerned, it is the height of irresponsibility not to have a plan for your own ghost.

EXACT CARD VOICE
Wealthier than ever thanks to exorbitant interest on wartime loans, the Orzhov only grew hungrier for more.

hero.thesis: Belonging becomes sacred when individual voice joins a greater living community.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Selesnya Conclave is a Commander deck that builds safety through numbers: make tokens, grow the board together, and turn collective strength into attacks that survive one-for-one answers. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.

Explore Convoke Community, Go-Wide Caretaking, Harmony and Preservation. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you want harmony, collective care, nature, preservation, consensus, and a community larger than private ambition.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It resists self-only ambition, conflict for its own sake, and procedure, debt, or force replacing belonging.
Check the boundary
Tokens, counters, enchantments, and pleasant company do not establish Selesnya by themselves; the distinguishing question is whether individual action yields to shared care and communal purpose.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The chorus
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents feel the deck as a board that becomes a community before it becomes a threat.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through belonging, protection, and many small pieces becoming one large promise.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
conclave, communal faith, and living civic body
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Convoke, populate, tokens, anthem effects, lifegain, and board protection

collective momentum, shared growth, and combat math that multiplies

REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Selesnya Conclave
A communal voice rooted in nature and shared purpose.
Belonging becomes sacred when individual voice joins a greater living community.
ART: TEMPLE GARDEN
DOSSIER DIRECTORY

FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Selesnya Conclave is a Commander deck that builds safety through numbers: make tokens, grow the board together, and turn collective strength into attacks that survive one-for-one answers. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Convoke Community, Go-Wide Caretaking, Harmony and Preservation. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether creatures pay for Convoke, a protected wide board carries communal care, or preservation keeps the community intact, then plan how the group rebuilds after a sweep.
TABLE CAUTION
Protect the engine, rebuild after wipes, and keep drawing cards so the table cannot answer every token wave.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you want harmony, collective care, nature, preservation, consensus, and a community larger than private ambition.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It resists self-only ambition, conflict for its own sake, and procedure, debt, or force replacing belonging.
Check the boundary
Tokens, counters, enchantments, and pleasant company do not establish Selesnya by themselves; the distinguishing question is whether individual action yields to shared care and communal purpose.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The chorus
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents feel the deck as a board that becomes a community before it becomes a threat.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through belonging, protection, and many small pieces becoming one large promise.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
conclave, communal faith, and living civic body
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Convoke, populate, tokens, anthem effects, lifegain, and board protection
TABLE EXPERIENCE
collective momentum, shared growth, and combat math that multiplies

hero.title: Simic Combine
hero.tagline: Life studied as an adaptive, improvable system.
hero.thesis: Simic treats nature as living systems to preserve, heal, study, adapt, and improve through biology, clade practice, and experimentation.

panels.text:

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Simic Combine is a Commander deck that adapts in motion: ramp, evolve through counters, and turn biological upgrades into flash-value pressure that improves whenever the game changes. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Living-System Value, Biological Adaptation, Clade Research and Pressure Response. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether ramp grows a living-system engine, counters express biological adaptation, or clade research changes the pressure response, then protect the organism that converts each upgrade into value.
TABLE CAUTION
Protect the engine, draw cards after each upgrade, and rebuild with counters when removal interrupts the experiment.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you study organisms, iterate pragmatically, and accept biological intervention when it helps life adapt, heal, or endure.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It resists untouched-nature absolutism, disposable-life engineering, and abstraction detached from living consequences.
Check the boundary
Counters, ramp, card draw, lands, and optimization do not establish Simic by themselves; look for biological study, adaptation, medicine, clades, or organism-level change.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The adapter
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents see the deck changing shape until yesterday's answer no longer fits today's board.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through adaptation, counters, ramp, and creatures that keep improving.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
biomancers, laboratories, evolutionary projects, and living infrastructure
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Graft, evolve, adapt, counters, ramp, card draw, and creature upgrades
TABLE EXPERIENCE
incremental growth, biological scaling, and threats that outgrow old answers

EXACT CARD VOICE

REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Simic Combine
Life studied as an adaptive, improvable system.
Simic treats nature as living systems to preserve, heal, study, adapt, and improve through biology, clade practice, and experimentation.
ART: SIMIC GUILDGATE
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE
IDENTITY & PLAY
COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Simic Combine is a Commander deck that adapts in motion: ramp, evolve through counters, and turn biological upgrades into flash-value pressure that improves whenever the game changes. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Living-System Value, Biological Adaptation, Clade Research and Pressure Response. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
GUILD SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether ramp grows a living-system engine, counters express biological adaptation, or clade research changes the pressure response, then protect the organism that converts each upgrade into value.
TABLE CAUTION
Protect the engine, draw cards after each upgrade, and rebuild with counters when removal interrupts the experiment.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
This may fit if you study organisms, iterate pragmatically, and accept biological intervention when it helps life adapt, heal, or endure.
Where it can pull too far
Watch for this tension: It resists untouched-nature absolutism, disposable-life engineering, and abstraction detached from living consequences.
Check the boundary
Counters, ramp, card draw, lands, and optimization do not establish Simic by themselves; look for biological study, adaptation, medicine, clades, or organism-level change.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The adapter
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Opponents see the deck changing shape until yesterday's answer no longer fits today's board.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Pressure through adaptation, counters, ramp, and creatures that keep improving.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
biomancers, laboratories, evolutionary projects, and living infrastructure
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Graft, evolve, adapt, counters, ramp, card draw, and creature upgrades
TABLE EXPERIENCE
incremental growth, biological scaling, and threats that outgrow old answers

EXACT CARD VOICE
Snaking remnants of nature directed by a body of thought and progress, the oracles embody all that is Simic.

EXACT CARD VOICE

hero.title: Lorehold College
hero.tagline: Leave no stone unturned.
hero.thesis: Lorehold treats history as something to recover, question, and put to use. Its scholars pore over artifacts and ancient texts, summon spirits as witnesses, and investigate what surviving records leave behind. White looks for preservation, precedent, and order; Red follows discovery, experience, and messy truths that refuse to stay neatly cataloged.

panels.text:
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Lorehold College is a Commander deck that starts with a historical angle, then lets the commander decide whether spirits, rebuilt relics, spells, or combat carry the lesson into play. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Spirit Witnesses / Graveyard-Leaves, Relic Reconstruction, History & Spells. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
COLLEGE SPELLCRAFT
Original Strixhaven supports cards leaving graveyards and Spirit tokens; Osgir owns artifact reconstruction; spells and combat belong only where a chosen commander supports them.
TABLE CAUTION
Choose one commander-led engine instead of treating every artifact, Spirit, or graveyard card as the same Lorehold package.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
You may find Lorehold in the urge to investigate old records, sites, relics, and spirits because they still have something to teach the present.
Where it can pull too far
Lorehold lives between careful preservation and discovery that can be adventurous, messy, or risky. A deck can lean toward either side, but history should be doing real work.
Check the boundary
Red-White action, artifacts, Spirits, or graveyard play alone do not make a deck Lorehold; the historical inquiry has to be part of the point.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
History in action
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Relics, Spirits, recovered spells, and remembered battles keep turning old resources into new problems.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Uncertainty, reuse, and reconstruction make old material feel active again.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
archaeologists, spirit scholars, and field researchers
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Cards leaving graveyards and Spirit witnesses in original Strixhaven; artifact reconstruction with Osgir; and commander-led spells or combat where that deck supports them
TABLE EXPERIENCE
History fights back: a Spirit becomes a witness, a relic becomes a tool again, or a recovered spell turns an old lesson into the next play.
CARDS THAT SOUND LIKE THIS

Lines of Magic flavor that sound like this reading.

Campus Renovation
EXACT CARD VOICE
Reconstructing the past is Lorehold's specialty.
VIEW CARD DETAILS

EXACT CARD VOICE

records.full_rendered_text:
REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Lorehold College
Leave no stone unturned.
Lorehold treats history as something to recover, question, and put to use. Its scholars pore over artifacts and ancient texts, summon spirits as witnesses, and investigate what surviving records leave behind. White looks for preservation, precedent, and order; Red follows discovery, experience, and messy truths that refuse to stay neatly cataloged.
ART: RAYMOND SWANLAND - VELOMACHUS LOREHOLD
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE
IDENTITY & PLAY
COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Lorehold College is a Commander deck that starts with a historical angle, then lets the commander decide whether spirits, rebuilt relics, spells, or combat carry the lesson into play. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Spirit Witnesses / Graveyard-Leaves, Relic Reconstruction, History & Spells. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
COLLEGE SPELLCRAFT
Original Strixhaven supports cards leaving graveyards and Spirit tokens; Osgir owns artifact reconstruction; spells and combat belong only where a chosen commander supports them.
TABLE CAUTION
Choose one commander-led engine instead of treating every artifact, Spirit, or graveyard card as the same Lorehold package.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
You may find Lorehold in the urge to investigate old records, sites, relics, and spirits because they still have something to teach the present.
Where it can pull too far
Lorehold lives between careful preservation and discovery that can be adventurous, messy, or risky. A deck can lean toward either side, but history should be doing real work.
Check the boundary
Red-White action, artifacts, Spirits, or graveyard play alone do not make a deck Lorehold; the historical inquiry has to be part of the point.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
History in action
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
Relics, Spirits, recovered spells, and remembered battles keep turning old resources into new problems.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Uncertainty, reuse, and reconstruction make old material feel active again.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
archaeologists, spirit scholars, and field researchers
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Cards leaving graveyards and Spirit witnesses in original Strixhaven; artifact reconstruction with Osgir; and commander-led spells or combat where that deck supports them
TABLE EXPERIENCE
History fights back: a Spirit becomes a witness, a relic becomes a tool again, or a recovered spell turns an old lesson into the next play.

hero.title: Prismari College
hero.tagline: Express yourself with the elements.
hero.thesis: The College of Elemental Arts holds that there is no difference between magic and art. Casting a spell is a performance, a canvas, a composition. Any elemental force can be a muse and a medium. The oldest argument in Prismari - technique versus expression - has never been resolved and never will be.

Start With This Commander Plan

COLLEGE SPELLCRAFT

TABLE CAUTION
Wait for shields to drop, hold protection, and make the big spell turn draw cards even if it gets answered.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
You may fit here when you want an idea or emotion to be felt through a chosen medium, and you accept practice, technique, and revision as part of authentic expression.
Where it can pull too far
The central tension is technique without feeling versus feeling without form; Prismari also resists usefulness or proof as the only standards of seriousness.
Check the boundary
Big spells, spectacle, novelty, or performance alone do not make a deck Prismari; expressive purpose and disciplined medium must do the work.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The crescendo
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
The table sees resources held for a turn where expression and impact arrive together.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Anticipation rises as the deck prepares one visible performance that may change the room at once.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
artists, elemental performers, and spellcraft prodigies
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Setup, protection, and copy effects converge on a chosen spell, while Elemental payoffs keep the performance present after it resolves
TABLE EXPERIENCE
a public rehearsal followed by one practiced sequence meant to become the turn everyone remembers

records.full_rendered_text:
REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Prismari College
Express yourself with the elements.
The College of Elemental Arts holds that there is no difference between magic and art. Casting a spell is a performance, a canvas, a composition. Any elemental force can be a muse and a medium. The oldest argument in Prismari - technique versus expression - has never been resolved and never will be.
ART: RAYMOND SWANLAND - GALAZETH PRISMARI
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE

CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES

FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Prismari College is a Commander deck that turns expression into the main event: build toward a big spell, copy the performance, and let elemental payoff make the table remember the turn. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Elemental Performance, Opus-Scale Spellcraft, Technique & Expression. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
COLLEGE SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether elemental performance, Opus-scale spellcraft, or technique and expression is the deck's center, then let the commander decide how spells and bodies carry it.
TABLE CAUTION
Wait for shields to drop, hold protection, and make the big spell turn draw cards even if it gets answered.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
You may fit here when you want an idea or emotion to be felt through a chosen medium, and you accept practice, technique, and revision as part of authentic expression.
Where it can pull too far
The central tension is technique without feeling versus feeling without form; Prismari also resists usefulness or proof as the only standards of seriousness.
Check the boundary
Big spells, spectacle, novelty, or performance alone do not make a deck Prismari; expressive purpose and disciplined medium must do the work.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The crescendo
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
The table sees resources held for a turn where expression and impact arrive together.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Anticipation rises as the deck prepares one visible performance that may change the room at once.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
artists, elemental performers, and spellcraft prodigies
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Setup, protection, and copy effects converge on a chosen spell, while Elemental payoffs keep the performance present after it resolves
TABLE EXPERIENCE
a public rehearsal followed by one practiced sequence meant to become the turn everyone remembers

hero.title: Quandrix College
hero.tagline: Math is magic.
hero.thesis: Quandrix treats mathematics as magical structure: patterns, fractals, symmetries, and abstract models reveal how nature works and how theory can become physical form.

panels.text:
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Quandrix College is a Commander deck that makes numbers outrun answers: ramp, double counters or tokens, and let each growth pattern become too large for the table to calculate. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Fractal Counters, Pattern Multiplication, Scalable Equations. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
COLLEGE SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether Fractal counters, pattern multiplication, or scalable equations are the deck's proof, then build one model deeply enough to compound.
TABLE CAUTION
Protect the doubler, draw cards before overextending, and rebuild with ramp when the table removes the key piece.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
You may fit here when you find beauty in proof, patterns, symmetry, models, precision, and problems whose underlying structure takes patience to reveal.
Where it can pull too far
Quandrix keeps discovery and construction in tension: is the pattern a natural force being found, or a mind-made model becoming real?
Check the boundary
Doubling, X spells, tokens, counters, or scaling alone do not make a deck Quandrix; mathematics, pattern, model, proof, or abstract structure must define the method.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The pattern engine
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
The table sees small, measured advantages begin to compound into a board state that is hard to calculate.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Each correct setup step makes the next ordinary answer less likely to be enough.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
mathematicians, theorists, fractal mages, and pattern seekers
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Ramp supplies the variables; a doubler or scalable payoff turns them into growth by proportion rather than simple addition
TABLE EXPERIENCE
a proof unfolding in public until the board has crossed from manageable quantities into a new scale
CARDS THAT SOUND LIKE THIS

Lines of Magic flavor that sound like this reading.

Additive Evolution
EXACT CARD VOICE
"Numbers have no limits. Why should nature?" —Emil, Quandrix fourth-year
VIEW CARD DETAILS
Golden Ratio
EXACT CARD VOICE
"When I look around, I see a world defined by patterns that still manages to defy them." —Kianne, Quandrix dean
VIEW CARD DETAILS
CARDS THAT PLAY LIKE THIS
Cards whose verified play patterns give you a concrete way to explore this reading.
Zimone, Infinite Analyst
WHY IT FITS IN PLAY
Zimone makes mathematical scaling visible: +1/+1 counters reduce an X spell's cost, and casting that spell adds more counters and creates a flying Fractal token.
VIEW CARD DETAILS

records.full_rendered_text:
REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Quandrix College
Math is magic.
Quandrix treats mathematics as magical structure: patterns, fractals, symmetries, and abstract models reveal how nature works and how theory can become physical form.
ART: RAYMOND SWANLAND - TANAZIR QUANDRIX
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE
IDENTITY & PLAY
COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Quandrix College is a Commander deck that makes numbers outrun answers: ramp, double counters or tokens, and let each growth pattern become too large for the table to calculate. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Fractal Counters, Pattern Multiplication, Scalable Equations. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
COLLEGE SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether Fractal counters, pattern multiplication, or scalable equations are the deck's proof, then build one model deeply enough to compound.
TABLE CAUTION
Protect the doubler, draw cards before overextending, and rebuild with ramp when the table removes the key piece.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
You may fit here when you find beauty in proof, patterns, symmetry, models, precision, and problems whose underlying structure takes patience to reveal.
Where it can pull too far
Quandrix keeps discovery and construction in tension: is the pattern a natural force being found, or a mind-made model becoming real?
Check the boundary
Doubling, X spells, tokens, counters, or scaling alone do not make a deck Quandrix; mathematics, pattern, model, proof, or abstract structure must define the method.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The pattern engine
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
The table sees small, measured advantages begin to compound into a board state that is hard to calculate.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Each correct setup step makes the next ordinary answer less likely to be enough.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
mathematicians, theorists, fractal mages, and pattern seekers
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Ramp supplies the variables; a doubler or scalable payoff turns them into growth by proportion rather than simple addition
TABLE EXPERIENCE
a proof unfolding in public until the board has crossed from manageable quantities into a new scale

"Numbers have no limits. Why should nature?" —Emil, Quandrix fourth-year

WHY IT FITS IN PLAY
Zimone makes mathematical scaling visible: +1/+1 counters reduce an X spell's cost, and casting that spell adds more counters and creates a flying Fractal token.

hero.title: Silverquill College
hero.tagline: Sharp style. Sharper wit.
hero.thesis: Silverquill treats language as action. Spoken, written, signed, rhetorical, and ink-and-light expression can lead, persuade, inspire, criticize, or pressure a room; the placement should require words, rhetoric, or word magic as the active method rather than generic black-white power.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Silverquill College is a Commander deck that makes language into pressure: pressure life totals, negotiate attacks, and turn counters or go-wide boards into visible social force. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Word-Magic and Rhetorical Influence, Leadership and Social Pressure, Visible Reputation. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
COLLEGE SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether word magic, leadership pressure, or visible reputation carries the deck's message, then use counters, Inklings, or attack incentives as the supporting method.
TABLE CAUTION
Sequence smaller threats first, hold a political answer, and protect the speaker that turns attacks into table pressure.

labels: Where it can pull too far
panels.text:
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
You may fit here when you lead, persuade, inspire, criticize, or pressure through precise spoken, written, signed, or magical expression.
Where it can pull too far
Silverquill asks whether eloquence becomes responsible leadership and uplift or intimidation, competition, and status pressure.
Check the boundary
Ambition, politics, counters, aggression, or charisma alone do not make a deck Silverquill; language or rhetoric must be doing the work.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The table speaker
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
The table has to account for who can be persuaded, criticized, rewarded, or made into the next public target.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Every attack and deal carries a visible social message, not just a combat calculation.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
orators, duelists, poets, and social power brokers
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Counters and Inklings make successful influence visible, while attack incentives and targeted interaction keep changing the public combat line
TABLE EXPERIENCE
alliances sharpen in public, and the deck's chosen speaker can turn attention into material advantage

EXACT CARD VOICE

EXACT CARD VOICE

records.full_rendered_text:
REVIEW MODE — DIRECT IDENTITY RENDER
Silverquill College
Sharp style. Sharper wit.
Silverquill treats language as action. Spoken, written, signed, rhetorical, and ink-and-light expression can lead, persuade, inspire, criticize, or pressure a room; the placement should require words, rhetoric, or word magic as the active method rather than generic black-white power.
ART: RAYMOND SWANLAND - SHADRIX SILVERQUILL
DOSSIER DIRECTORY
START HERE
IDENTITY & PLAY
COMMANDER BROWSING STARTS
CARD SIGNALS
MANA NOTES
MAZE DISCOVERY
FOCUS VIEW
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Silverquill College is a Commander deck that makes language into pressure: pressure life totals, negotiate attacks, and turn counters or go-wide boards into visible social force. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Word-Magic and Rhetorical Influence, Leadership and Social Pressure, Visible Reputation. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
COLLEGE SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether word magic, leadership pressure, or visible reputation carries the deck's message, then use counters, Inklings, or attack incentives as the supporting method.
TABLE CAUTION
Sequence smaller threats first, hold a political answer, and protect the speaker that turns attacks into table pressure.
TEST THE FIT
A useful self-check
You may fit here when you lead, persuade, inspire, criticize, or pressure through precise spoken, written, signed, or magical expression.
Where it can pull too far
Silverquill asks whether eloquence becomes responsible leadership and uplift or intimidation, competition, and status pressure.
Check the boundary
Ambition, politics, counters, aggression, or charisma alone do not make a deck Silverquill; language or rhetoric must be doing the work.
HOW THIS PLAYS
AT THE TABLE
ROLE
The table speaker
HOW OPPONENTS READ IT
The table has to account for who can be persuaded, criticized, rewarded, or made into the next public target.
EMOTIONAL PRESSURE
Every attack and deal carries a visible social message, not just a combat calculation.
IN PLAY
LORE ROLE
orators, duelists, poets, and social power brokers
MECHANICAL EXPRESSION
Counters and Inklings make successful influence visible, while attack incentives and targeted interaction keep changing the public combat line
TABLE EXPERIENCE
alliances sharpen in public, and the deck's chosen speaker can turn attention into material advantage

EXACT CARD VOICE
"I've lived too long in my father's shadow. It's time to find my own light." —Killian, Silverquill mage-student

WHY IT FITS IN PLAY
Breena makes social influence change combat: attacks against a leading opponent can reward the attacker with a card while making Breena larger.

hero.title: Witherbloom College
hero.tagline: Study life and death as living essences.
hero.thesis: Life and death are living essences to study and use through brewing, healing, harm, death-facing magic, and practical craft.

panels.text:
START HERE

Use these Commander starting points to turn this identity into decks, cards, and searches you can compare.

Start With This Commander Plan
One way to explore Witherbloom College is a Commander deck that treats life and death as one economy: spend life, feed Pests, drain the table, and use Infusion lines to turn biology into power. Adjust the budget, complexity, and table role to fit your deck.
POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS
Explore Essence Exchange, Remedies and Poisons, Field Biology and Cost. Compare these lanes to see which one matches the deck you want to build.
COLLEGE SPELLCRAFT
Choose whether essence exchange, remedies and poisons, or field biology and cost is the deck's center, then use life totals and small bodies to sustain that line.
TABLE CAUTION
Protect the drain engine, buy time with life gain, and rebuild through Pests when the table removes your outlet.
